title: Find a hitch with profile scopes: time the suspects, read the report's hitches, fix the heaviest game scope
note: A frame-time spike: wrap the suspects in profile_scope!, read the profile report's hitches and fix the heaviest game scope.
intent: A hitch is a frame over its line. Before changing code, time the suspects: wrap each part you could blame (AI, a generator, a pathfinding batch, a spawn wave) in genex::profile_scope!("name") and count what grows with genex::profile::counter. Names are 1 to 48 bytes of a-z, 0-9, _, . and -, and scopes are write-only, so the checksum never changes. Then read state().volatile.profile (top lists the 8 heaviest scopes by p95; game: true marks yours) or ask preview.frameProfile for a report: each kept hitch names its frame, its cause (cpu, gpu or pacing) and its heaviest scopes. A cpu hitch topped by a game scope is yours: spread the work over ticks, cap it per tick, or build it once in on_reset. A gpu hitch wants fewer draws or a lighter preset (arm nodes to see which pass). A pacing hitch is the machine or the compositor, not the build. Measure again after the fix: the same scope's p95 must fall.
port: The facet that owns the work owns its scope and its counter; scope names stay unique across facets (prefix them with the facet).

evidence.note: profile_scope! and profile::counter are write-only; volatile.profile summarizes the last 120 frames with the 8 heaviest scopes; the profile verb reads a ProfileReport v2 with every kept hitch.
